cells.tense: The structure holds, and what is inside it is growing at its own pace.
cells.act: release it on purpose, not by losing it
cells.ask: Finish the piece that is yours to finish, then take your hands off it — set it down on purpose, because it's done, not because you gave up.
cells.core:
You've built something with a shape to it — a routine, a team, a room where things get made — and it stands. What's inside is growing at its own pace, and your part is mostly to keep conditions steady rather than hurry anything along. The care has stopped costing you more than it gives.

The grip is loosening where it should. One part of this no longer needs your hand on it, and you know which part. Finish the piece that is yours to finish and then step back from it. Setting something down on purpose is what keeps a thing you built standing while you're somewhere else.
cells.sheetLine: The structure holds, and the growing is not yours to push.
cells.place: where a workable structure gets made

cells.tense: You will be gripping a future version of this thing tight enough that today cannot get a word in.
cells.act: take the next step with only enough light for that step
cells.ask: Take one step whose ending you can already picture. Stop when you reach it; the step after stays unplanned until it shows up.
cells.core:
The care here works when you set the conditions and then give the thing inside its own time. Your side of it stays steady, and none of the work is aimed at one particular day.

What's happening instead is bracing. You can picture where this should be in six months, so you're arranging today around a picture nobody can check — nudging, correcting, tightening the frame until it stops being a place things grow and becomes a place you stand guard in. Take one step the light already reaches, its ending visible, and stop there. Let the rest stay dark until it arrives. What you are protecting survives the waiting.
cells.sheetLine: The care has tightened into guarding a future you can't see yet.
cells.place: where a workable structure gets made

cells.tense: The structure is up, and it has been some time since anything inside it grew.
cells.act: move toward the thing you actually want
cells.ask: Give your next free hour to something inside this structure you truly want — no plan made first, no conditions met beforehand. Go before you feel ready.
cells.core:
The structure is standing — routines kept, things handled — and nothing inside it has grown in a while. You carry it up by yourself and call that being independent, and it does keep the whole thing quiet. Nothing in it is being tended.

What you want is still there; it's just been kept off the list. Choose the part of this you would regret losing most, and walk toward it with your next free hour. That hour is the whole of the instruction — not a plan for it, not the version of it you'd earn once everything else is done. It can be small. It needs to be something you actually want.
cells.sheetLine: The structure stands. Nothing in it is growing.
cells.place: where a workable structure gets made

cells.tense: Others come to you as the one who holds this together, and the keeping is not something you chose.
cells.act: stop holding what no longer serves
cells.ask: Pick one duty that landed on you and didn't get chosen. Stop carrying that piece; if a week passes and it's visibly undone, that's what happened.
cells.core:
People bring you the parts that need steadying, and you steady them, and nobody asks whether that was the deal. You didn't sign up for the role; it got handed to you and you kept doing it, so it stuck. The steadying is real. What's missing is your hand in the decision.

Not the whole of it — a piece. Pick one duty that landed on you rather than one you picked up on purpose, and set it down. If it goes undone and someone notices, you'll have the fact of it out where you can see it, and a say in whether you take it back up.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying something you didn't agree to carry.
cells.place: where a workable structure gets made

attempts.check: The record hands me two channels — Nurturing on Structure, the seat on Mind — and I am reading 'looking after what you are building' as structures you have made: a team, a household, a routine, a draft. The reader could reasonably say no, my care goes to people, not projects — the reads still land because care is care, but the asks are pitched at a thing you're making, and a person will have to translate. If the read is wrong, the ask still stands: letting go of one thing you're gripping is useful whether the grip is a plan or a person. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line where I decide what they feel while holding on — I've kept the mechanism and left their interior alone.
